subject.title: [Feature]: read-only channel mode (inbound only, no outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw own a stable no-outbound channel/account contract here as a shared channel/plugin API, a WhatsApp-specific account `readOnly` mode, or delegate this kind of passive WhatsApp monitoring to an external isolation layer such as wacli?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a durable config/security boundary and related PRs show competing viable ownership shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve WhatsApp account readOnly
options.body: Define `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.readOnly` as the first stable no-outbound contract and keep hooks-only/no-agent behavior on the separate design issue.

options.title: Design shared channel contract
options.body: Add a plugin/channel SDK no-outbound capability so WhatsApp, Signal, and future channels can enforce the invariant consistently.

options.title: Delegate to external isolation
options.body: Reject core/plugin config for now and document an external passive-monitoring path if maintainers decide channel plugins should stay conversational.

recommendation.title: Approve WhatsApp account readOnly
recommendation.body: Define `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.readOnly` as the first stable no-outbound contract and keep hooks-only/no-agent behavior on the separate design issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The related PR discussion explicitly routed WhatsApp expertise to this person, and they contributed the adjacent hook-config narrowing commit.
